left_margin_red_stars.description: A series of red 8-pointed stars positioned in the left margin, each marking the beginning of a new text section or paragraph grouping. Approximately 8 stars are visible, evenly spaced vertically down the left margin. Each star has a central red dot or circle with 8 points radiating outward. They function as visual paragraph markers or section flags, equivalent to illuminated capitals in other manuscripts.
left_margin_red_stars.color: Deep red (vermilion or red lead). The stars are the ONLY color element on this otherwise monochrome text page — making them extremely visually prominent against the cream parchment. No fill color other than red; the points and body are solidly red-painted.

right_margin_red_star.description: A smaller red star or asterisk mark at the right margin, approximately mid-folio. Possibly an annotation or correction marker added by a reader. Similar red pigment to the left stars but smaller and less formal.
right_margin_red_star.color: Same deep red as left margin stars. Smaller scale.

top_green_smear.description: A faint green wash visible at the very top edge of the folio. This is likely bleed-through or offset from a painted illustration on an adjacent page, not an intentional element of f105v itself.
top_green_smear.color: Pale/faded medium green. Very faint — probably transferred pigment.

ruled_line_bottom.description: A light horizontal ruled line visible beneath the dense text block, approximately at y=940. This line may mark the boundary of the writing area or separate a final sub-section.
ruled_line_bottom.color: Pale brown/lead point ruling line. Very faint.

text_blocks_mapping.description: f105v is one of the most text-dense folios in the Voynich Manuscript. It contains a single uninterrupted paragraph of 38 lines (loci 1–38) covering virtually the entire parchment surface from top to bottom. There are NO illustrations, NO label zones, NO bisections. The only decorative elements are the red star markers in the left margin. The text is written in dark brown-black ink throughout, with a consistent baseline and x-height. Left margin is approximately x=100 (after the star markers); right margin extends to approximately x=920. The red stars appear to divide the text visually into approximately 8 sections of 4–6 lines each, though the transcription treats the entire block as one continuous paragraph.

isolated_zones.status: Non-text decorative markers — exclusive red color on otherwise monochrome folio
isolated_zones.description: The 8 red stars occupy x=28–95, distributed across y=45–960. They are the SOLE color element on this text-only folio. No text overlaps them; the paragraph text begins at x=100, leaving a clear gutter for the stars. Their deep red color is visually identical to the red pigment used for vessels in f88r and other balneological illustrations, suggesting the same pigment source.

isolated_zones.status: Incidental transfer — not part of f105v composition
isolated_zones.description: The pale green at top (y=0–38) is likely pigment transfer from an adjacent illustrated page. The medium-green color matches Voynich botanical leaf illustrations. It does not affect any text lines.
